notes:
Definitions

  • Distance = actual path length (scalar, always positive). Displacement = shortest straight-line change in position (vector; can be zero even when distance is not).
  • Speed = distance/time (scalar); Velocity = displacement/time (vector). Average speed $\geq$ magnitude of average velocity, with equality only when motion is one-directional along a straight line.

Equations of motion (uniform acceleration $a$)

  • $v = u + at$
  • $s = ut + \frac12at^2$
  • $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$
  • Distance in the $n^{th}$ second: $s_n = u + \dfrac{a}{2}(2n-1)$

  • On a v–t graph, area below the time axis counts as negative displacement; total distance travelled is the sum of the magnitudes of all such areas.

Relative velocity

  • $v_{AB} = v_A - v_B$ (vector subtraction). Same direction → subtract magnitudes; opposite directions → add magnitudes.

Vertical motion under gravity

  • Taking upward as positive, $g$ acts as $-g$. For a body thrown up with speed $u$: time of flight $T = 2u/g$; maximum height $H = u^2/2g$; it returns to the point of projection with speed $u$ (in the absence of air resistance).

Average speed for two-part journeys

  • Equal distances at speeds $v_1, v_2$: average speed $= \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}$ (harmonic mean).
  • Equal time intervals at speeds $v_1, v_2$: average speed $= \dfrac{v_1+v_2}{2}$ (arithmetic mean). Do not confuse the two cases.

Calculus form

  • $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$, $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}$, and $v\,dv = a\,dx$.

Exam tip

KCET usually sets 1–2 questions from this chapter — typically a direct equations-of-motion or free-fall numerical, sometimes a graph-reading or relative-velocity question. Fix sign conventions before substituting numbers.

questions.q: A car starting from rest accelerates uniformly at 2 m s$^{-2}$. Its velocity after 5 s is
A car starting from rest with uniform acceleration $a = 2$ m s$^{-2}$ covers a distance in the first 5 s equal to
questions.explanation: $s = ut + \frac12at^2 = 0 + \frac12\times2\times25 = 25$ m.

questions.q: A stone dropped from a tower reaches the ground in 4 s. The height of the tower is
questions.explanation: $h = \frac12gt^2 = \frac12\times10\times16 = 80$ m.

questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration 4 m s$^{-2}$. The distance covered by it in the 3rd second is
A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 30 m s$^{-1}$. The time after which it returns to the point of projection is
questions.explanation: $T = \dfrac{2u}{g} = \dfrac{2\times30}{10} = 6$ s.

questions.q: A ball thrown vertically upward with speed 20 m s$^{-1}$ rises to a maximum height of
Two cars A and B travel in the same direction at 72 km h$^{-1}$ and 54 km h$^{-1}$ respectively. The velocity of A relative to B is
questions.explanation: Same direction, so relative velocity $= 72 - 54 = 18$ km h$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Two trains move in opposite directions at 60 km h$^{-1}$ and 40 km h$^{-1}$. The speed of one train relative to the other is
questions.explanation: Opposite directions, so relative velocity magnitudes add: $60 + 40 = 100$ km h$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A person walks 4 km east and then 3 km west, the whole trip taking 1 hour. His average velocity is
questions.explanation: Net displacement $= 4 - 3 = 1$ km (east); average velocity $= 1/1 = 1$ km h$^{-1}$ (average speed would be 7 km h$^{-1}$).

questions.q: A position–time (x–t) graph of a particle is a straight line inclined to the time axis. The particle is moving with
questions.explanation: A constant slope on an x–t graph means the velocity ($dx/dt$) does not change, i.e. uniform velocity.

questions.q: A particle's velocity rises uniformly from 0 to 20 m s$^{-1}$ in 4 s and then stays constant at 20 m s$^{-1}$ for the next 4 s. The total displacement in 8 s is
questions.explanation: Area under v–t graph: triangle $\frac12\times4\times20 = 40$ m plus rectangle $4\times20 = 80$ m, total $120$ m.

questions.q: The position of a particle is $x = 2t^2 + 3t + 1$ (in metres, $t$ in seconds). Its velocity at $t = 2$ s is
The velocity of a particle is $v = 3t^2 - 6t$ (SI units). Its acceleration at $t = 2$ s is
A car covers the first half of a distance at 20 km h$^{-1}$ and the second half at 30 km h$^{-1}$. Its average speed for the whole journey is
questions.explanation: Equal distances: average speed $= \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2} = \dfrac{2\times20\times30}{50} = 24$ km h$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A car travels the first half of the total TIME of a journey at 20 km h$^{-1}$ and the second half of the time at 30 km h$^{-1}$. Its average speed is
questions.explanation: Equal time intervals: average speed is the arithmetic mean $= \dfrac{20+30}{2} = 25$ km h$^{-1}$.
questions.tip: Equal distances -> harmonic mean; equal times -> arithmetic mean.

questions.q: A car moving at 20 m s$^{-1}$ is brought to rest by brakes that produce a uniform deceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$. The stopping distance is
questions.explanation: Using $v^2 = u^2 - 2as$ with $v=0$: $s = \dfrac{u^2}{2a} = \dfrac{400}{10} = 40$ m.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically downward with an initial speed of 5 m s$^{-1}$ from the top of a 100 m tower. The time it takes to reach the ground is
questions.explanation: $100 = 5t + \frac12(10)t^2 \Rightarrow 5t^2+5t-100=0 \Rightarrow t^2+t-20=0 \Rightarrow t = 4$ s (taking the positive root).

questions.q: For any moving particle, which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: The straight-line displacement can never be longer than the actual path length; they are equal only for one-directional straight-line motion.

questions.q: A particle's velocity decreases uniformly from 10 m s$^{-1}$ to $-10$ m s$^{-1}$ over 5 s (v–t graph is a straight line through zero at $t=2.5$ s). The net displacement in these 5 s is
questions.explanation: Area above the axis (0 to 2.5 s) $= \frac12\times2.5\times10 = 12.5$ m; area below the axis (2.5 to 5 s) $= -12.5$ m. Net displacement $= 12.5 - 12.5 = 0$ m (though total distance travelled is 25 m).

questions.q: A velocity-time graph that is a horizontal line parallel to the time axis represents motion with
questions.explanation: A horizontal v-t line means velocity does not change with time, i.e. zero acceleration and uniform (constant, non-zero) velocity.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from the top of a tower. A second stone is dropped from the same point 2 s later. How far apart are the two stones 5 s after the first stone was dropped?
questions.explanation: First stone falls for 5 s: $\frac12(10)(5^2)=125$ m. Second stone falls for $5-2=3$ s: $\frac12(10)(3^2)=45$ m. Separation $=125-45=80$ m.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with speed 10 m s$^{-1}$ from the top of a tower 15 m high. The time taken to reach the ground is
questions.explanation: Taking up as positive: $-15 = 10t - 5t^2 \Rightarrow t^2-2t-3=0 \Rightarrow (t-3)(t+1)=0 \Rightarrow t=3$ s.

questions.q: A train of length 150 m moving at 54 km h$^{-1}$ overtakes another train of length 100 m moving at 36 km h$^{-1}$ in the same direction. The time taken to completely cross it is
questions.explanation: Relative speed $=54-36=18$ km h$^{-1}=5$ m s$^{-1}$. Total length to be covered $=150+100=250$ m. Time $=250/5=50$ s.

questions.q: The area under an acceleration–time graph between two instants gives the
questions.explanation: Since $a = dv/dt$, the area under the a-t graph, $\int a\,dt$, equals the change in velocity over that interval.

questions.q: A particle moves with velocity $v = 2t^3$ (SI units). Its displacement between $t=1$ s and $t=2$ s is
questions.explanation: $x=\int v\,dt = \frac{t^4}{2}$. Displacement $= \frac{2^4}{2}-\frac{1^4}{2} = 8-0.5 = 7.5$ m.

questions.q: A particle starts from rest with uniform acceleration $a$. A graph of displacement $s$ versus $t^2$ is a straight line through the origin whose slope equals
questions.explanation: Since $s=\frac12at^2$, plotting $s$ against $t^2$ gives a straight line through the origin with slope $s/t^2=a/2$.

questions.q: A car moving at 20 m s$^{-1}$ has a driver whose reaction time is 0.5 s. After the driver reacts, the brakes produce a deceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$. The total distance travelled before the car stops is
questions.explanation: Reaction distance $=20\times0.5=10$ m. Braking distance $=u^2/2a=400/10=40$ m. Total $=10+40=50$ m.

questions.q: On a velocity–time graph, if the graph crosses the time axis, the particle
options: has zero acceleration at that instant
questions.explanation: The velocity changes sign at the crossing point, meaning the particle momentarily comes to rest and then moves in the opposite direction.

questions.q: The average velocity of a particle over a time interval equals its instantaneous velocity at every instant within that interval only when the particle moves with
questions.explanation: Only when velocity itself does not change (constant velocity) is the instantaneous velocity the same at every instant and hence equal to the average.

questions.q: A body falls freely from rest. The ratio of distances covered in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd seconds of its fall is
questions.explanation: $s_n \propto (2n-1)$, so distances in successive seconds are in the ratio $1:3:5$, independent of $g$.

questions.q: Two cars 100 m apart move towards each other with speeds 10 m s$^{-1}$ and 15 m s$^{-1}$. They meet after
questions.explanation: Closing speed $=10+15=25$ m s$^{-1}$. Time to meet $=100/25=4$ s.

questions.q: An escalator moves upward at 1 m s$^{-1}$. A man climbs it at 0.5 m s$^{-1}$ relative to the escalator, in the same direction. His speed relative to the ground is
questions.explanation: Velocities in the same direction add: speed relative to ground $=1+0.5=1.5$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A ball thrown vertically upward with speed $u$ passes a certain height $h$ twice: once going up (at time $t_1$) and once coming down (at time $t_2$). Which relation always holds?
questions.explanation: $h = ut - \frac12gt^2$ is a quadratic in $t$ with roots $t_1, t_2$; the sum of roots is $-b/a = 2u/g$, which is exactly the total time of flight, and is independent of $h$.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: A body can have zero velocity and non-zero acceleration simultaneously
Displacement is always greater than or equal to distance travelled
A body can have zero acceleration and non-zero velocity simultaneously
questions.explanation: The magnitude of displacement is always less than or equal to distance travelled, never the other way round; the other three statements are true (e.g. a ball at its highest point, or motion at constant velocity).

questions.q: The slope of a velocity–time graph at any instant gives the instantaneous
questions.explanation: Slope of the v-t graph $= dv/dt$, which is the instantaneous acceleration.

questions.q: A particle has initial velocity 5 m s$^{-1}$ and constant acceleration $-2$ m s$^{-2}$. Its velocity at $t = 4$ s is
questions.explanation: $v = u+at = 5+(-2)(4) = 5-8 = -3$ m s$^{-1}$; the negative sign shows the particle has reversed direction.

questions.q: From the top of a tower, ball A is thrown upward with speed $u$ and, at the same instant, ball B is thrown downward with the same speed $u$. Which is correct about their speeds on reaching the ground (ignore air resistance)?
options: B reaches the ground with greater speed
Both reach the ground with the same speed
A reaches the ground with greater speed
Cannot be determined without knowing the height
questions.explanation: Ball A returns to the point of projection with the same speed $u$ directed downward as ball B started with; from there on, both fall identically, so they reach the ground with equal speeds.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward with initial speed 20 m s$^{-1}$. The height above the point of projection at which its speed becomes 10 m s$^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh \Rightarrow 100 = 400 - 20h \Rightarrow h = 15$ m.

questions.q: A body has initial velocity 5 m s$^{-1}$ and uniform acceleration 2 m s$^{-2}$. The distance covered by it in the 4th second is
Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance has only magnitude (no direction), so it is a scalar; displacement, velocity and acceleration are all vectors.
